text:
Maya: quick thought — for the automatic fallback rollout UI, can we add a lightweight "contingency nudge" panel that shows why a request hit a fallback and what the soft-mode was? small, read-only, and linkable :eyes:
Jon: sounds useful. do you mean at the per-route rollout page or global policy page?
Maya: per-route initially. goal: devs can see a compact trace like: `primary -> latency spike -> routed to cheap-quantized -> confidence warn` and a single-click jump to the audit entry. no huge playback UI, just the signal + one-sentence cause.
Riley: telemetry-wise we should include the triggering metric (p95, error-rate, kv-cache-miss). need to pick a standard schema. also, sampling: we can't log full requests by default. propose: audit record = {event_id, trigger_metric, model_variant, sampling_ratio, conf_score_bucket, trace_link}.
Sasha: UI note: show the nudge on top of rollout timeline as a small orange pill — "soft-fallback active" — clicking expands the short trace Maya mentioned. keep it non-intrusive.
Jon: API question: how does this interact with current rollout API? We already have /rollouts/:id/events which stores events, but payloads are inconsistent. if we add fields we should keep backwards compatible. example proto (very rough):
```
POST /rollouts/:id/events
{
  "type": "fallback_trigger",
  "t": 1680000000,
  "trigger_metric": "latency_p95",
  "metric_value": 2400,
  "variant": "gptxx-8q",
  "sampling_ratio": 0.02,
  "reason_code": "latency_sla",
  "audit_link": "https://console.redwood/audit/evt-1234"
}
```
Riley: +1 to that. also add `signal_snippet` (string) for a short human summary, e.g. "p95 2400ms > 2000ms threshold". keep it 160 chars max.
DeployBot: deploy status: canary rollout r-2026-03-17 -> triggered fallback at 2026-03-17T14:12:03Z (reason: latency_p95) :warning:
Maya: nice — the bot example proves the UI flow. UX ask: have the nudge include an inline CTA: "simulate no-fallback" which runs a dry-run and shows expected success rate. purely preview, no changes.
Sasha: design question: do we surface sampling_ratio? It helps debug but might be noisy. maybe only show if < 1.0 with a tooltip: "only sampled subset of requests are audited".
Jon: ops concern: audit storage costs. if we keep sampling default at 1% for fallback events we can keep costs low. but product might want longer tail retention for enterprise customers. we should expose retention per-tenant.
Erin (Product): from product POV, the key is trust. teams want to quickly understand: did fallback cost us quality? the contingency nudge should link to a small eval: sample prompt set perf delta (fast diff view). not full eval, just 5 example prompts. thoughts?
Riley: we can attach a short eval summary if we run an automated micro-eval on sampled requests. else it's empty. keep it opt-in.
Maya: final checklist from UX side: 1) compact pill on rollout timeline, 2) single-line human summary, 3) audit link, 4) simulate-dry-run button, 5) small eval snapshot if available.
Sasha: will mock up a 2-state pill (active / historical) and a small flyout. I'll post wires tomorrow. :party_parrot: 
Jon: I'll add API schema to the rollout events endpoint and ensure backward compatibility. agree on sampling_ratio and short `signal_snippet`.
Riley: I'll add telemetry mapping doc: what maps to `trigger_metric`, how to bucket `conf_score`, and recommended sampling defaults.
Maya: ok — owners: Sasha (UX mock), Jon (API), Riley (telemetry), Maya (product-prototype + acceptance). timeline: POC wires + API spec by EOD Fri?
Erin (Product): that timeline works. thanks all.
Maya: cool — one more thought: add a small audit badge for tenants with stricter retention/policy so support can see why retention differs. small follow-up later.
Jon: noted. I'll add an optional `tenant_retention_policy` tag to events for enterprise accounts.
Maya: awesome. ending thread — will watch for Sasha wires.
